title: Closed immersions descend over qcqs scheme limits
statement: Work over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ with schemes [def-pc-scheme] and algebraic spaces [def-trf-algebraic-space], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. A space is quasi-compact if it admits a surjective etale atlas from a quasi-compact scheme, and quasi-separated if its diagonal is quasi-compact; a morphism is quasi-compact when its pullback by any affine scheme has quasi-compact source. Finite presentation means quasi-compact, quasi-separated, and locally of finite presentation on etale scheme charts [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. A closed immersion is representable and is a closed immersion on every scheme test [def-weil-closed-immersion]. An affine morphism is representable and has affine source after every affine scheme test. Fibre products are sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Let $J$ be a small nonempty directed set, $(T_j)_{j\in J}$ an inverse system of quasi-compact quasi-separated schemes with affine transition morphisms, and $T=\varprojlim_j T_j$. Fix $j_0\in J$, finitely presented algebraic spaces $Y_{j_0},Z_{j_0}$ over $T_{j_0}$, and a $T_{j_0}$-morphism $h_{j_0}:Y_{j_0}\to Z_{j_0}$. Write $h_j$ for its base change to $T_j$ for $j\ge j_0$, and $h$ for its base change to $T$. If $h$ is a closed immersion, then $h_j$ is a closed immersion for some $j\ge j_0$ and for every later stage. The bases $T_j$ need not be affine.

source.place: Tag 0850 (lemma-descend-closed-immersion), in Situation 084W (situation-descent-property), with local finite type of the stage morphism supplied by Tag 05WT (spaces-morphisms-lemma-finite-presentation-permanence); persistence by representability and scheme base change

proof.text: First the hypotheses needed for the affine-base descent lemma hold before restricting the base. By [lem-sfb-space-fp-qcqs-source], $Y_{j_0}$ and $Z_{j_0}$ are quasi-compact and quasi-separated, since their structure maps are finitely presented and $T_{j_0}$ is qcqs. The structure map of $Y_{j_0}$ is locally of finite presentation, and that of $Z_{j_0}$ is locally of finite type: on charts a finitely presented algebra $R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]/(r_1,\ldots,r_m)$ is generated by the images of the $x_i$. Apply [lem-sfb-space-relative-lfp-permanence] with $X=Y_{j_0}$, $Y=Z_{j_0}$ and $Z=T_{j_0}$. Thus $h_{j_0}$ is locally of finite presentation, in particular locally of finite type by the same finite-generator observation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation].

Choose a finite affine open cover $T_{j_0}=\bigcup_{a=1}^r W_{a,0}$: the affine neighbourhoods in the definition of scheme form an open cover, and quasi-compactness selects finitely many [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme]. Empty bases allow $r=0$. Restrict the directed set to $j\ge j_0$; it remains small, nonempty and directed. Put $W_{a,j}=T_j\times_{T_{j_0}}W_{a,0}$ and $W_a=T\times_{T_{j_0}}W_{a,0}$. These are the inverse-image open subschemes and cover $T_j$ and $T$, respectively. Each $W_{a,j}$ is affine by the assumed affineness of $T_j\to T_{j_0}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-limit-affine-transition], the restricted transitions are affine and $W_a=\varprojlim_{j\ge j_0}W_{a,j}$.

For each $a$ put $Y_{a,0}=Y_{j_0}\times_{T_{j_0}}W_{a,0}$, $Z_{a,0}=Z_{j_0}\times_{T_{j_0}}W_{a,0}$ and $h_{a,0}=h_{j_0}|_{W_{a,0}}$. The scheme $W_{a,0}$ is qcqs by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]. Apply [lem-sfb-space-qcqs-source-products] to these fibre products: both restricted spaces are qcqs, since all three factors are qcqs. Moreover $h_{a,0}$ is locally of finite type. Indeed this is restriction of $h_{j_0}$ to the inverse image of an open of the base; on etale scheme charts it just restricts the same local finite-presentation ring charts established in step 1. No affineness of intersections of the $W_{a,0}$ is used.

source.place: Tag 084W (situation-descent-property), restricting to affine opens; spaces-morphisms Tag 073B (lemma-quasi-compact-quasi-separated-permanence)

proof.text: We will use persistence of closed immersions under arbitrary algebraic-space base change, which here follows directly from the scheme-test definition. If $i:E\to F$ is a closed immersion and $F^\prime\to F$ is any map of algebraic spaces, then for every scheme $C\to F^\prime$ there is the canonical identification $(E\times_FF^\prime)\times_{F^\prime}C=E\times_FC$ of sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. The right side is a scheme closed in $C$ by the defining hypothesis on $i$. This proves representability and the closed-immersion test for the new morphism. When the test is further pulled back between schemes, [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence](b) gives precisely the same closed immersion. In particular the limit restriction $h_a$ of $h$ over $W_a$ is a closed immersion.

source.place: Tag 0850 (lemma-descend-closed-immersion), restriction of the limit map; scheme tests and base change

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-space-descend-closed-immersion] separately to each affine inverse system $(W_{a,j})_{j\ge j_0}$ and $h_{a,0}$. Step 2 supplies its affine bases and limit; step 3 supplies its qcqs source and target and local finite type; step 4 supplies its closed-immersion limit. It gives $j_a\ge j_0$ where $h_{a,j_a}$ is a closed immersion. Directedness gives one $j\ge j_0,j_1,\ldots,j_r$ by induction on the finite list (start at $j_0$ and take an upper bound with each $j_a$ in turn). For this $j$, every $h_{a,j}$ is a closed immersion by step 4, since it is the pullback of $h_{a,j_a}$ to $W_{a,j}$. If $r=0$, take $j=j_0$.

source.place: Tag 0850 (lemma-descend-closed-immersion), applied on the finite affine base cover

proof.text: We now glue without assuming representability of $h_j$. Choose an etale scheme atlas $V\to Z_j$, which exists by [def-trf-algebraic-space]. The inverse images $V_a$ of $W_{a,j}$ are open subschemes covering $V$. Open immersions of schemes are etale [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-etale]; composing their representable etale maps with the atlas is etale by [lem-trf-space-chartwise-etale-permanence]. Hence the composites $V_a\to Z_j$ are jointly surjective etale maps from schemes. By the sheaf fibre-product identification [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers], $Y_j\times_{Z_j}V_a=Y_{a,j}\times_{Z_{a,j}}V_a$. This is a scheme closed in $V_a$, because $h_{a,j}$ is a closed immersion. Apply [lem-sfb-space-closed-immersion-atlas-locality] to this family. It gives that $h_j$ is representable and is a closed immersion on every scheme test, hence a closed immersion as required. If the family is empty, its target is empty and the same locality assertion applies. Finally for $k\ge j$ the map $h_k$ is the base change of $h_j$ to $T_k$; step 4 proves the claimed persistence at every later stage.

Step 2: a finite affine cover; W_{a,j} is affine by the item's own definition of affine morphism, and W_a is the limit of the W_{a,j} by the 01YX inverse-image clause. Step 3: the restricted spaces are qcqs by the 073B fibre-product clause, with no affine-intersection assumption. Step 4: base change of a closed immersion, elementary from the scheme-test definition. Step 5: every hypothesis of the existing affine-base node lem-sfb-space-descend-closed-immersion is met, followed by a finite common upper bound. Step 6: atlas gluing with V_a covering V, the étale composite from 02GP and the chartwise-étale lemma, and 03M4 atlas locality, which does not assume representability. Edge cases checked: empty base or source, P^1 base, members of the cover that are empty at the limit. No duplicate found: the affine-base node is reused, the pbc version is scheme-only, and trf cover-descent is an atlas statement without a limit. The only citer (proper-noetherian-approximation) uses nonaffine qcqs base stages. No cycle; proof_deps equal the union of the step uses; no SGA.
